parameters.text:
=You write link-building e-mails for {{ $json.business }} ({{ $json.domain }}): short, specific, honest messages from one person to the editor or author of one website. Each prospect gets a SEQUENCE — the first e-mail and the follow-ups — which a person will read, edit and send from their own mailbox. Journalists and editors delete pitches that are irrelevant, promotional or feel mass-produced; hand-made, specific e-mails get two to three times the replies.

WHAT WE KNOW (use only these facts; put anything the owner must confirm in [brackets])
{{ $json.facts }}
Homepage: {{ $json.home }}
Sign every e-mail exactly: {{ $json.signer }}

PROSPECTS
{{ ($json.jobs || []).map(j => j.n + '. ' + j.prospect_domain + ' [' + j.angle + ']\n   their page: ' + (j.page_url || '-') + (j.page_title ? ' — "' + j.page_title + '"' : '') + '\n   evidence: ' + (j.evidence || '-') + (j.dead ? '\n   dead link on their page: "' + (j.dead.anchor || '') + '" → ' + j.dead.url : '') + (j.competitors_named.length ? '\n   they name: ' + j.competitors_named.join(', ') : '') + '\n   writing to: ' + j.contact + (j.deadline ? '\n   deadline: ' + j.deadline : '') + '\n   our page to offer: ' + j.target_url + (j.target_title ? ' — "' + j.target_title + '"' : '') + ' (link text if they ask: ' + (j.anchor_hint === 'title' ? 'its title or a description in their words' : j.anchor_hint === 'as before' ? 'as it was' : 'our brand name') + ')').join('\n\n') }}

Angle by kind:
- broken: one link on their page is dead (name it exactly: its text and URL). Say so first — that is the useful part — then offer our page as a current page on the same subject, in one sentence on what it covers.
- lost: their page used to link to us; the link is gone. Ask kindly whether it could be restored, give our current URL.
- mention: they mention us without a link. Thank them in one line, ask whether the mention could link to our homepage.
- list / ai_list / ai_source (a list): their list names similar providers but not us. One sentence on why we fit their readers, then the facts they would need (what we do, for whom, where). Offer a logo or a 50-word description.
- resource: a resources / useful-links page on our topic. Offer our page as an addition, one sentence on what it adds for their readers.
- gap / comp_new / ai_source (an article): they link to similar resources on this topic. Offer our page as a useful addition for their readers, or expert input (a quote in [brackets] for the owner to confirm, a data point from the facts, a correction).
- podcast: a podcast on our topics that takes guests. Offer the signer as a guest: name the show and quote what they say about guests (or the episode kind you mean), then two or three specific things they could talk about that their listeners would want (only from the facts above), and the homepage once. End with one question ("would an episode on that suit your listeners?"). No media kit, no list of topics longer than three, no "I'd love to share my story".
- digest: a journalist's request that arrived in a media digest (HARO / Source of Sources). Treat it exactly like press, and answer the address the digest gives.
- press: a journalist's request. The first e-mail IS the answer: 120-200 words of expert input that answers exactly what they asked (practical, specific, [brackets] for any figure or claim the owner must confirm), who is answering (the signer) and why they know; the homepage once. Subject: "Re: " + their request in a few words.

Rules for every e-mail:
- First e-mail: 80-120 words (press / digest 120-200), plain text, no markdown, no bullet lists unless giving facts for a list. Subject 36-50 characters, specific to their page (never "Quick question" or "Collaboration").
- The first sentence is about THEIR page — quote or name the evidence. No compliments you cannot back with the evidence, no fake familiarity ("I've been reading your blog for years"), no "I hope this finds you well".
- Exactly one link: our page to offer. Never write "backlink", "link building", "dofollow", "SEO", "DA" or "DR"; never ask for specific link text or a keyword; never offer money, a link swap or a guest post; never mention AI assistants or rankings.
- Do not add an unsubscribe line or an address: the app adds the sender's details and opt-out line to every e-mail.
- Follow-up 1 (sent 4 working days later in the same thread, 40-60 words, no subject): one NEW useful detail — a specific section of our page that fits their page, or an offer that makes it easy (a short description, a logo, a correction). Not "just bumping this".
- Follow-up 2 (8 working days after that, 30-55 words, no subject, the last one): ask whether someone else handles their page ("who would be the right person?") or offer the easiest alternative, and say plainly you will not write again.
- press / digest: only ONE follow-up (3 working days later, 30-50 words), and none if the deadline has passed by then.
- TWO subjects for the first e-mail of every sequence, in two different styles, both 36-50 characters and both specific to this prospect:
  `subject` (style A) names the thing you found on their page or in their request ("Dead link on your VAT resources page");
  `subject_b` (style B) is the one question you are asking, in their words ("Add a UAE e-invoicing guide to your list?").
  A person approves whichever is sent; half the batch goes out with each style so we can see which one gets more replies. Neither may
  contain a word from the forbidden list above or anything left in [brackets].
- Write the business name exactly as it stands in the facts above, every time (never the website address, never a lower-case version of it).
- Say nothing about the business that the facts above do not carry: no accreditation, certification, licence, partnership, award, client count,
  years, size or price unless it is in the facts. Where a figure or a proof point would help, write it as [Owner: confirm — …] so the owner fills it in.
- One clear ask per e-mail (a single question), and nothing is asked of a list of accredited, approved or certified providers unless the facts
  say the business holds that accreditation — those lists are joined by applying, not by a pitch.
- If the evidence shows a prospect is not a fit (unrelated topic, a competitor's own site, their bare homepage, a page that sells links), do not write — list it under "skip" with the reason.

Return ONLY JSON:
{"sequences": [{"n": 1, "subject_b": "", "steps": [{"step": 0, "subject": "", "body": ""}, {"step": 1, "body": ""}, {"step": 2, "body": ""}]}], "skip": [{"n": 2, "reason": ""}]}

// Copy of each report HTML named index.html for the PDF renderer (Gotenberg requires that exact file name); one item per site.
return $input.all().map(item => { const doc = (item.binary || {}).data; if (!doc) return item; return { json: item.json, binary: { ...(item.binary || {}), html: { ...doc, fileName: 'index.html', mimeType: 'text/html', fileExtension: 'html' } } }; });

parameters.content:
## SEO Agent — Link Builder (v4.13, LINK_BUILDER_SPEC.md)
**Every Monday 11:00** (after the Backlink Monitor 07:30 and AI Growth 09:30) and on demand (*Manual Run* `{{ domain | site_id, free_only?, callback_url?, request_id? }}`, started by **SEO Agent — Link Builder API** `POST /webhook/seo-link-builder`). Per site with `link_builder` on (`seo_monitors`, default on).
**New opportunities** (free): journalist requests (#journorequest on Bluesky, matched to the topics), **journalist digests** (HARO / Source of Sources, read from the customer's own mailbox by the web app and written here as `digest` prospects — nothing arrives until a mailbox is connected), **podcast shows that take guests** (monthly: a free podcast directory → the show's RSS feed → the show's own website; pitched only when it is on topic, still publishing, says it takes guests and has a contact on its own domain), resource pages (web search), dead links on resource / list pages, our old URLs from the Wayback Machine that now 404 (redirects), the listings checklist (own and competitors' pages, member lists, guessed profiles); monthly **competitors' broken backlinks** and their **most-linked pages** (DataForSEO, ≈ $0.07 + ≈ $0.02 a competitor) — the second gives the **linkable-asset ideas** (data study / free tool / template / definitive guide), each tied to the competitor pages that prove it and the referring domains they hold, and never a promise of links. **Every prospect** (also the Backlink Monitor's and AI Growth's) qualified (gone / blocked / sells links / language / already linking), with the evidence to quote, up to 3 contacts, the recipient's country, **our page and the link text** (topic match × position band × links needed, paced). **Outreach Sequence Writer** (Claude): ≤ 10 sequences a week (first e-mail + 2 follow-ups; journalists: 1), then the **draft gate** (*LB Draft QA*, L2): claims against the facts on file, no bracket left to fill, the address on their own domain, a real quote from their page, one link to the page we chose on the canonical host, length and one clear ask, the words we never use, the business name as the site model has it — a draft that fails is held as `needs_edit` with its reasons. **Two subjects a batch** (L7): the writer gives every sequence a second subject in the other style, the drafts take the two in turn (A, B, A, B …) and the app shows the reply rate per style — with **no verdict under 30 first e-mails per variant**. Nothing is sent here: the **web app** sends from the customer's own mailbox after approval.
Rows: `seo_link_outreach`, `seo_link_prospects` (new kinds), `seo_listings`, `seo_link_impact` (what each won link did, vs the site's other pages), `seo_cache` linkbld:; report + callback `link_builder`.
**The week as a PDF** (L3): *LB Doc* writes the whole week as one printable document — what to do this week, every opportunity with its qualification, the contacts found on the prospects' own domains, our page and the link text per prospect, each drafted sequence with its status (a held one with the reasons), the listings checklist, the redirects, what the links and the page changes did, and where every figure came from — and *Render PDF LB* turns it into a PDF through Gotenberg: attached to the e-mail and carried in the callback, so the app offers it like the other reports' PDFs. A renderer failure never fails the run (the HTML document goes out instead).
